description: Source of truth for the sf update command surface used by the tool-saasfoundry skill. Each entry maps an intent JSON field to its corresponding --flag on `sf update`. Both plan-update.sh and the skill's discovery conversation read this file — keep them in sync by editing here, never by hardcoding flag names elsewhere. sf update is ADD-ONLY today; module removal is not yet supported by the CLI.

targetProfile.description: Add the missing managed capability so an eligible harness-only or stack-only project becomes full. V1 never removes a capability or changes an existing stack topology.

projectDescription.requiresWhen: targetProfile is full and the technical stack is absent; otherwise the CLI derives a description from projectName

structure.requiresWhen: targetProfile is full and the technical stack is absent

dbSetup.requiresWhen: targetProfile is full and the technical stack is absent

emailService.requiresWhen: targetProfile is full and the technical stack is absent

addModules.description: Comma-separated list of modules to add. Values must come from `sf modules list --json` and must not already appear in .saasfoundry.json.

dryRun.description: Preview the plan without mutating files. Pair with json=true for stable machine-readable stdout. Always recommend this first.

json.description: Emit one stable versioned JSON object on stdout. Use with --dry-run; diagnostics go to stderr.

acceptTemplateUpdates.description: Auto-apply non-conflicting template updates without prompting.

conflictStrategy.description: How three-way merge conflicts are handled. save-new preserves both sides, keep ignores upstream changes, replace overwrites local edits.

mailersendApiKey.requiresWhen: addModules includes email or targetProfile is full with emailService mailersend

mailersendSenderEmail.requiresWhen: addModules includes email or targetProfile is full with emailService mailersend

mailersendSenderName.requiresWhen: addModules includes email or targetProfile is full with emailService mailersend

s3Setup.requiresWhen: addModules includes storage or targetProfile is full and the technical stack is absent

analytics.requiresWhen: targetProfile is full and the technical stack is absent

pwa.requiresWhen: targetProfile is full and the technical stack is absent

srsBackend.description: Backend hosting the SRS workspace. V1 supports Notion only.

srsParentPageInput.description: URL or ID of the parent page (Notion) that will host the SRS root page. The page must be shared with the Notion integration.

dryRun.true: Always recommend `--dry-run` first so the user sees the template-merge plan before files are mutated. Run the real command only after explicit approval.
dryRun.false: Only skip dry-run if the user explicitly says 'just do it' and the addition is one small module with no template merge risk.

conflictStrategy.save-new: Default — the safest option: conflicting files are written as `.saasfoundry.new` next to the originals so the user can diff and reconcile.
conflictStrategy.keep: Choose when the user has significant local edits they do not want touched by a template update.
conflictStrategy.replace: Choose only when the user wants the latest upstream version and is okay losing local edits to conflicting files.

modules.harness: Compatibility spelling for a stack-only project becoming full. Prefer targetProfile=full in new plans so status, CLI and guidance share one capability transition.
modules.email: Recommend adding when the app now needs transactional email (password reset, invites, receipts). Requires a mailersend API key.
modules.storage: Recommend adding when the app needs file uploads (logos, user docs). Docker setup for local dev, credentials for staging/prod.
modules.analytics: Recommend adding when tracking user activity or business metrics becomes relevant. Self-hosted Umami, production-only.
modules.srs: Recommend adding when product requirements should be centralised for AI agents (User flows, Functional Requirements). V1 bootstraps a Notion workspace under a parent page shared with the Notion integration.
modules.sf-skill-context7: Recommend adding when the project relies on third-party libs and needs up-to-date doc retrieval for the AI agent.
modules.sf-skill-atlassian: Recommend adding when issues/pages live in Jira or Confluence and the AI agent should read/write them.
modules.sf-skill-notion: Recommend adding when product specs or knowledge base live in Notion.
modules.sf-skill-figma: Recommend adding when design hand-off goes through Figma files.
